props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about Vidiyum Mun, a time-loop mystery at a beach party on ECR, Chennai, into two particle effects: a sand scuff on each of Hari's footsteps, and moths around the string lights at night. Add fixture previews, headless tests and a price check.

beats.role_note: Game, both effects, their jobs, the event and the condition (CHANGE-BRIEF.md A.4 #8, B.1).
beats.narration_text: Vidiyum Mun is a time loop at a beach party in Chennai. Effect A, a sand scuff, fires each time Hari's foot lands, to tie him to the ground. Effect B, moths at the string lights, is ambience: only while it's night, before five A M, minute seventeen forty.

props.title: The game, two effects, two triggers
props.excerpt:
The scuff should fire once for every actual footfall while Hari is walking.

The moths should only appear when:
- The game phase is `NIGHT`.
- The game clock is before 5:00 AM, represented as minute `1740` on the extended overnight clock.

beats.role_note: Emission / process / draw in the SoftDust node. Paired result B04 (r0 strip).
beats.narration_text: Every particle system has three parts. Emission: when and where. Ten particles at once, one shot, from a small box at the foot. Process: how each moves and changes. Speed, gravity, damping, a scale curve, a colour ramp. Draw: what each looks like. This quad mesh, twelve centimetres, facing the camera.

beats.role_note: The trigger: foot contact from walked distance; one new instance per contact. Paired result B06.
beats.narration_text: The game has no footstep signal, so the trigger makes one. It reads how far Hari has walked, and counts a landing every point eight four metres. Each landing gets a new scuff instance, freed after one point one five seconds. New, not restarted, so bursts overlap: at most four.

beats.role_note: The controller: reads state, drives emitting only, restart on edges, hide after 2.4 s. Paired result B20.
beats.narration_text: The controller reads the game state, never writes it. Night, before minute seventeen forty, and visible: emitting. Turned on or shown again: restart, so preprocess refills the group. When it ends, emitting stops, and two point four seconds later the group hides.

props.title: Start, stop, hide: the moth controller

beats.role_note: Headless CPU price (cost log) and the GPU price (Shriram's Visual Profiler screenshots, TEST-REPORT A6.6).
beats.narration_text: The prices. Headless CPU per frame, against an empty-scene control of five point eight microseconds. Effect A adds thirteen point two, inside its budget. Effect B adds three point three, within noise: the dummy renderer runs no GPU particle process. And the Visual Profiler read zero milliseconds of GPU on every row, so GPU time could not be measured here. With vsync off, both effects together cost about point one three to point two eight milliseconds. Per-effect budgets: not confirmed.

beats.role_note: Agent mistakes caught; Claude's readings Shriram overruled (A6.8); what headless can't show.
beats.narration_text: What the agents got wrong. Step one ran out of turns and left a draft over its line limit. Step two's preview drew a reconstructed background, not the real level. A test couldn't catch a double fire. The moth texture was haze. The wiring plan called ambience a feedback loop. And agents tried commands outside their allow list. Claude was overruled too: r zero too fast, the cotton balls, and three rounds of invisible moths.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Brief one particle effect for one event in your game, with timings, before any node exists. Ask Claude for the scene, and a test that reads every setting back. Then use a Godot three name, and watch it fail. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: I wrote a brief for one particle effect on one event in my game: amount, lifetime, ramps and when it fires. Build the scene, and a headless test that loads it and reads every setting back against my brief. I predict a Godot 3 property name will fail it.
output: You write the brief and the timings.
Rename one property: it must fail.
